questions.stem: The refractive index is the maximum at which of the following surface:
questions.solutionHtml:
Centre of the lens
  • The relaxed eye has an approximate optical power of 60 diopters (D) (ie, its focal length is 16.7 mm in air), with the corneal power being about 40 D or two-thirds of the total power.


Parsons Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 275

questions.stem: Asteroid hyalinosis is composed of which of the following:
questions.solutionHtml:
Calcium
  • Histologically, asteroid bodies are rounded structures that stain positively with alcian blue and positively with stains for neutral fats, phospholipids, and calcium.
  • The bodies stain metachromatically and exhibit birefringence. Occasionally, asteroid bodies will be surrounded by a foreign body giant cell, but the condition is not generally associated with vitreous inflammation.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 323

Removal of foreign body

questions.stemHtml: Identify the instrument depicted in the given Image:
questions.solutionHtml:
Synoptophore
  • A haploscope is an optical device for presenting one Image to one eye and another Image to the other eye.
  • The word is often used interchangeably with stereoscope, but it is more general than that.
  • A stereoscope is a type of haploscope, but not vice versa. The word has more currency in the medical field than elsewhere, where it refers to instruments designed to test binocular vision.
  • These instruments include Worth's amblyoscope and the synoptophore.
  • Commonly laparoscopic employ front-surface mirrors placed at different angles close to the eyes to reflect the Images into the eyes.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 378

questions.stemHtml: Identify the pathology depicted in the given Image:
questions.solutionHtml:
Telecanthus
  • Telecanthus, or dystopia canthorum, refers to the increased distance between the inner corners of the eyelids (medial canthi), while the inter-pupillary distance is normal.
  • This is in contrast to hypertelorism, in which the distance between the whole eyes is increased.
  • The average interpupillary distance is 60–62 mm, which corresponds to an intercanthal distance of approximately 30–31 mm
  • Associated with systemic conditions such as Down syndrome, fetal alcohol syndrome, cri du Chat syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome, Turner syndrome, Ehlers–Danlos syndrome, Waardenburg syndrome


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 422

questions.stem: Which of the following does not handle free radicals in lenses?
questions.solutionHtml:
VIT. A
  • The ocular lens, which is continually exposed to light and ambient oxygen, is at high risk of photooxidative damage resulting in cataracts.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 367

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man comes to the physician because of bilateral blurry vision and difficulty driving at night that has been worsening progressively over the past 5 months. He has hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hyperlipidemia. His hemoglobin A1c concentration is 8.9 mg/dL. A slit lamp shows cloudy opacities of the lenses bilaterally. The patient's eye condition is most likely due to increased activity of which of the following enzymes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldose Reductase
  • This patient's physical examination shows bilateral cataracts, most likely due to his poorly-controlled diabetes mellitus.
  • Aldose reductase catalyzes the reduction of glucose to sorbitol, which is subsequently oxidized to fructose by the sorbitol dehydrogenase enzyme.
  • At normal blood glucose levels, only a small part of glucose is metabolized via this polyol pathway.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 242

questions.stem: An 8-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his parents for a blurry vision for the past 2 months. He is at the 97th percentile for height and the 25th percentile for weight. Physical examination shows joint hypermobility, a high-arched palate, and abnormally long, slender fingers and toes. Slit lamp examination shows superotemporal lens subluxation bilaterally. This patient's findings are most likely caused by a defect in which of the following structural proteins?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fibrillin
  • This patient presents with features of Marfan syndrome (i.e., tall stature, high-arched palate, arachnodactyly, joint hypermobility, and superotemporal lens subluxation).
  • Marfan syndrome is caused by an autosomal dominant mutation in the fibrillin-1 gene, which encodes fibrillin, an extracellular matrix glycoprotein that forms a supportive sheath around elastin.


Parson’s Disease of the Eye, 23rd Edition, Page No. 371
